note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. The method: Rewrite ordinary numbers in the form a x 10^n with 1 <= a < 10. Earlier backups were dropped for doing this instead: Multiplies a quantity by a number of grams in scientific notation instead of converting numbers to a x 10^n form.

lines.text: Move the decimal point so that $1 \le a < 10$: three places, so $n = 3$.
Move the decimal point one place right to get $2.7$, so $n = -1$.
A billion is a thousand million, so it is $10^3 \times 10^6$.

steps.title: Find the relative frequency of red

lines.text: Relative frequency $= \dfrac{\text{number of reds}}{\text{number of spins}}$.
